title: comfy install --cpu/--amd resolved generic PyPI torch because --fast-deps ignores the vendor flag
description: CLOSED 2026-07-31 - the fix this card owns SHIPPED and is positively proven. _provisionUvEngine passed --fast-deps for every vendor except --m-series; comfy-cli DependencyCompiler ignores the vendor flag and resolves generic PyPI torch, which on Linux pinned the entire CUDA 13 stack. FIX: --fast-deps is now added only for --nvidia (routes/engine.js), where a generic resolve is what we want. PROVEN LIVE on Linux 2026-07-31: the [comfy-install] stage consults download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu, resolves torch-2.13.0+cpu / torchaudio-2.11.0+cpu / torchvision-0.28.0+cpu, and NO nvidia-*, triton or cuda-* package appears in that stage at all. requirements.compiled is absent from the engine root, confirming DependencyCompiler is off the path. THE CARD WAS RETITLED TO THAT SCOPE BEFORE CLOSING. It was originally named after the SYMPTOM ("--cpu installs pull the whole CUDA stack"), and that symptom survives because a LATER stage undoes this fix: custom-node requirements reinstall CUDA torch over the CPU one. Closing under the symptom title would have been a false done. THE RESIDUAL SYMPTOM IS OWNED BY MPI-413, now the umbrella for the whole install-what-we-chose problem.

attention.reason: Its own half is now POSITIVELY proven (+cpu wheels, torch 2.13.0+cpu). Card still cannot close until MPI-413 stops the custom-node stage overwriting it.
